title: mathgraph/freeze_bench.py main() crashes: hardcoded artifact names idx_deploy/idx_mathlib_only don't exist
description:
README.md's "The shipped benchmark" section (~line 1198) says bench_release/
is "produced on demand by running python -m mathgraph.freeze_bench" with no
caveats. That command crashes on a real corpus built by `mathgraph setup`.

REPRODUCED (this session):

  cd /tmp && MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data \
    uv --project /workspace run python -m mathgraph.freeze_bench

  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/workspace/mathgraph/freeze_bench.py", line 152, in main
      deploy = {r["name"] for r in load("idx_deploy")["rows"]}
    File "/workspace/mathgraph/index.py", line 425, in load
      with gzip.open(os.path.join(out_dir, "index.pkl.gz"), "rb") as fh:
  FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'idx_deploy/index.pkl.gz'

ROOT CAUSE: freeze_bench.py:152-153 calls:

    deploy = {r["name"] for r in load("idx_deploy")["rows"]}
    mathlib = {r["name"] for r in load("idx_mathlib_only")["rows"]}

Two bugs at once:
1. Wrong artifact names. Nowhere else in the codebase are indices called
   idx_deploy or idx_mathlib_only -- setup_cmd.py builds idx_mathlib,
   idx_full, idx_blueprint (grep mathgraph/setup_cmd.py, mathgraph/cli.py:67
   CORPORA list). This container's actual /workspace/mathgraph-data/artifacts/
   contains idx_full, idx_mathlib, idx_blueprint, idx_elaborated -- never
   idx_deploy or idx_mathlib_only. grep -rn "idx_deploy\|idx_mathlib_only"
   mathgraph/ finds these two names ONLY inside freeze_bench.py, nowhere else.
2. No path prefix at all. `load()` (mathgraph/index.py:424) takes a directory
   and looks for <dir>/index.pkl.gz inside it. Everywhere else in the codebase
   (cli.py's `_art()`, tests/test_corpus.py's `idx()`) joins the name onto
   os.path.join(MATHGRAPH_DATA, "artifacts", name) first. freeze_bench.py
   passes the bare string with no join at all, so even an index named
   correctly would only be found if you happened to be running from inside a
   directory containing an idx_deploy/ subfolder.

This was already discovered once and worked around, not fixed: closed bead
mathgraph-q3z's own reproduction steps (see `bd show mathgraph-q3z`) say:
  "uv --project /workspace run python -c ... fb.main(...)" only worked after
  "idx_full and idx_mathlib symlinked to the names it expects (idx_deploy,
  idx_mathlib_only)" via `ln -sf .../idx_full idx_deploy && ln -sf
  .../idx_mathlib idx_mathlib_only`.
q3z's scope was narrowly the CARD template's hardcoded 175/174 (fixed) and it
explicitly left this naming/path mismatch as a workaround, not a fix. No bead
was filed to actually fix it, and README's "shipped benchmark" section
(reworded by mathgraph-036 and mathgraph-y1e) still describes running the
bare command as if it works standalone -- it does not.

FIX: change freeze_bench.py:152-153 to load the real artifact names
(idx_full, idx_mathlib) via a path built from MATHGRAPH_DATA/artifacts,
consistent with cli.py's `_art()` helper or tests/test_corpus.py's `idx()`
helper (both do os.path.join(art_dir, name)). Then re-run the exact
reproduction command above against a real corpus and confirm it writes
bench_release/{tasks.jsonl,scorer.py,README.md} without a symlink workaround.

EVIDENCE THAT CLOSES THIS: `python -m mathgraph.freeze_bench` (no symlinks,
no monkeypatching) run against a real MATHGRAPH_DATA corpus writes
bench_release/ successfully, and the printed {"present": N, "absent": M}
matches tasks.jsonl's actual row counts.
close_reason: Fixed: freeze_bench.py now loads idx_full/idx_mathlib via MATHGRAPH_DATA/artifacts path (matching cli.py's _art() helper), instead of nonexistent idx_deploy/idx_mathlib_only with no path prefix. Verified: python -m mathgraph.freeze_bench run standalone (no symlinks, no monkeypatching) against a real MATHGRAPH_DATA corpus writes bench_release/{tasks.jsonl,scorer.py,README.md}; printed {present:176,absent:174} matches tasks.jsonl's actual row counts. Full suite: 85/85 passed (0 failures -- the previously-documented 175-vs-176 baseline failure was already fixed by other uncommitted work in the tree, unrelated to this bead). Filed mathgraph-dgd for the same bug pattern found in bench_pfr.py, adapt.py, bench_dense.py (out of this bead's scope).

title: README.md:262 absent-arm status breakdown (170/4/0) does not reproduce; command now gives 168/6/0
description:
README.md:254-262 (Absent arm table) publishes 'status breakdown | 170 unmatched, 4 ambiguous, 0 matched' for the PFR absent arm. Running the exact command README.md:291-292 points to as the reproducer for this section:

uv run python -m mathgraph.bench_pfr '{"deploy": "mathgraph-data/artifacts/idx_full", "mathlib_only": "mathgraph-data/artifacts/idx_mathlib", "pattern": "mathgraph-data/blueprints/pfr/blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex", "len_pivot": 0.75, "mod_weight": 0.1, "typ_weight": 0.15, "prefix_weight": 0.85, "title_boost": 2.5}'

...and reading the '.absent.status' field of the output gives {"matched": 0, "ambiguous": 6, "unmatched": 168} -- not {unmatched: 170, ambiguous: 4} as published. Confirmed 3x in this session: repeated 2x back-to-back (identical output both times) and once more under PYTHONHASHSEED=0/1/42 (all three gave the same 168/6/0), so it is not a hash-randomization artifact. glob.glob() calls in bench_pfr.py/cli.py are all wrapped in sorted(), ruling out directory-iteration-order nondeterminism too. The on-disk index artifacts (mathgraph-data/artifacts/idx_full, idx_mathlib) are dated 2026-08-03, unchanged since before the README commit that published these numbers (591d4a9, 2026-08-08), and mathgraph-data is pinned to the same git commit as this repo -- so this is not a case of the corpus having moved since the number was written; the same inputs give a different output in this environment right now.

Both totals sum to 174 (170+4=168+6=174) and the headline claims are unaffected either way: correct_abstention=1.0 and false_match_rate=0.0 reproduce exactly regardless of the split. Only the ambiguous-vs-unmatched classification of 2 statements differs.

What would close this: determine why the same command against the same index gives a different ambiguous/unmatched split than what's published (candidates to check: float/BLAS nondeterminism from numpy on different CPU architectures -- this container is linux-aarch64 -- affecting a near-threshold tie-break in the ambiguous-classification logic in align.py; or the number was mistyped/miscopied into the README rather than pasted from actual output). Then either fix the classification logic to be deterministic across environments, or correct the README number to match a verified re-run, whichever the root cause calls for. Do not just edit the README number without first establishing which of those two it is.
notes: Investigated: repeated runs (7 total across sessions), PYTHONHASHSEED variation, and float32-vs-float64 rescoring of the near-threshold statements all agree on 168/6/0. align.py and bench_pfr.py's arm_absent loop are byte-identical since before both the 167/7 and 170/4 figures were ever published; idx_mathlib predates the commit that published 170/4. No mechanism found that would make 170/4 reproduce. Concluded transcription error in README, not a code bug. Fixed README.md:262 to 168/6/0 with provenance note. Full evidence in sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-p14.md.
close_reason: Fixed: README corrected to the verified, repeatedly-reproducing status breakdown (168 unmatched, 6 ambiguous, 0 matched), with provenance recorded inline and in sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-p14.md. No code bug found after ruling out hash-seed, iteration-order, and float32/64 precision as causes.

title: README.md:16 & 280-281: combined-arm calibration-sweep figure ('3 answers out of 349') has no reproducing command and 349 is arithmetically the old arm sizes
description:
README.md:16 (top-of-file summary) and README.md:280-281 ("Calibration sweep over both arms
combined") both state: best achievable precision is "~67%, on 3 answers out of 349".

349 = 175 (old/stale present-arm n) + 174 (absent-arm n). Both addends are individually
documented and tested elsewhere in this repo, and the present-arm one has been independently
confirmed stale (now 176, not 175 -- see mathgraph-3gu, mathgraph-etj, mathgraph-1f3). If the
combined-arm denominator is genuinely just present_n + absent_n, the current value should be
176 + 174 = 350, not 349.

I searched for a script or test that actually computes this combined-arm sweep (as opposed to
each arm's numbers individually, which bench_pfr.py / cmd_bench do reproduce):

  grep -n "def \|sweep\|calibrat" mathgraph/cli.py         # no sweep command
  grep -rln "calibrat" mathgraph/*.py                       # bench_dense.py, cli.py,
                                                              # freeze_bench.py, evaluate.py,
                                                              # verify.py -- none combine PFR
                                                              # present+absent into one
                                                              # precision sweep
  # evaluate.py's `sweep`/`sweep_zero_false`/`graph_arms` operate on the 439-pair non-PFR
  # blueprint corpus (idx_blueprint/idx_mathlib, see evaluate.py:95-107's own comment: "the arms
  # GRAPH_THRESHOLDS is fitted on... 439 harvested blueprint pairs"), NOT the PFR 175/176/179
  # statements this README section is about.

So there is currently no command in the codebase that reproduces "3 answers out of 349" (or
"67%") from scratch -- same class of gap as mathgraph-2zj (verify-layer table) and coupled to
the "175+174" figure baked into mathgraph/freeze_bench.py's CARD (mathgraph-q3z) and README:1105
(mathgraph task for that line), which is the same underlying pair of arm sizes.

I deliberately did NOT try to recompute "3 answers"/"67%" myself -- that requires implementing
an actual combined precision-vs-coverage sweep over both PFR arms together, which is measurement
work, not triage, and this file explicitly warns against fabricating numbers.

Work needed (whoever picks this up should choose one):
(a) Write the combined-arm sweep (likely: build `recs` the way `evaluate.sweep_zero_false` or
    `evaluate.sweep` do, but from bench_pfr's present+absent arm results together) as a
    reproducible script or test, re-run it, and update both README.md:16 and README.md:280-281
    with the new denominator (350, if it's a straight sum -- but verify precision/answer-count
    fresh rather than assuming only the denominator moved) and the resulting precision/answer
    count.
(b) If that sweep genuinely was a one-off manual analysis that isn't meant to be routinely
    reproducible, label both mentions with when/how it was produced (date, commit, or "manual
    analysis, not scripted") so a reader can tell it's a frozen measurement rather than a live
    claim.

This is the single most load-bearing negative number in the README (it's in the first paragraph
and directly supports "neither benchmark admits a trustworthy operating point" -- do NOT soften
that conclusion while fixing this; if the recomputed precision/answer-count changes, report the
new number plainly, same hedge.

Evidence that closes this: either (a) a script's output matching the updated text verbatim, or
(b) the added provenance label.
notes: Resolved via option (a): wrote combined_precision_sweep() in mathgraph/bench_pfr.py (exhaustive threshold grid over both PFR arms' pooled (coverage,margin) records, max precision tie-broken by answer count, no floor). Re-measured against idx_full/idx_mathlib (the actually-built corpora): present n=176, absent n=174, combined n=350 -- confirms the bead's 176+174=350 hypothesis exactly. Fresh sweep gives precision=1.0 (100%) on 3/3 answers, not the old ~67%/3/349. Verified the shipped GRAPH_THRESHOLDS and Aligner defaults both answer 0 on this pool (old figure wasn't 'shipped thresholds, scored'), and a zero-false-match-constrained optimum gives 75%/4 (also above 67%), so 100%/3 isn't a fluke of my tie-break rule. Updated README.md:16 and the combined-arm-sweep paragraph (~line 280) with the new number, the reproducing command, and explicit provenance for why 349 was stale (175 pre-scanner-fix present arm + 174 absent). Kept the 'no operating point that is both useful and trustworthy' hedge verbatim in substance -- 3/350 = 0.9% coverage, still not usable, argued explicitly in the handoff rather than softened. Test suite: 76 run, 1 pre-existing failure (176 != 175, known baseline), nothing else broken. Filed mathgraph-ek7 for an unrelated drift I noticed while verifying (present-arm recall@1 18.2% in README vs 18.8/18.9% measured/pinned by tests) -- did not fix, out of scope. Full detail in sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-aec.md.
close_reason: Combined-arm sweep now exists in code (mathgraph/bench_pfr.py:combined_precision_sweep), reproducing command documented in README, both mentions (line 16, ~line 280) updated with the freshly measured 100% on 3/350 and provenance for why the old 67%/349 was stale. Evidence: script output matches README text verbatim (verified). Test suite at documented known-good state (76 run, 1 pre-existing failure).

title: README.md:250-259 PFR absent-arm section: '174 of 175' is internally inconsistent AND stale; status breakdown (167/7/0) no longer matches current run (170/4/0)
description:
README.md:250-259 ("Absent arm") has two separate, independently-confirmable problems.

1. Internal arithmetic inconsistency, visible from the text alone: line 252 says
   "only mathlib indexed, so 174 of 175 statements have no correct answer" (denominator 175,
   implying 1 statement already has an answer in mathlib alone). But the status-breakdown table
   two lines later (line 259) reads "167 unmatched, 7 ambiguous, 0 matched" -- which sums to
   174, not 175. The paragraph's own denominator doesn't match its own table's total. This is
   true regardless of what the code currently produces.

2. Current-code drift, confirmed by running the actual absent-arm evaluation with the
   thresholds the README's numbers are calibrated with (GRAPH_THRESHOLDS, matching
   tests/test_corpus.py's `Abstention` test setup exactly):

   MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -c "
   from mathgraph.bench_pfr import blueprint_blocks, arm_absent
   from mathgraph.align import Aligner
   from mathgraph.index import load
   from mathgraph.cli import GRAPH_THRESHOLDS
   import os
   ART = os.path.join(os.environ['MATHGRAPH_DATA'], 'artifacts')
   blocks = blueprint_blocks('/workspace/mathgraph-data/blueprints/pfr/blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex')
   al = Aligner(load(os.path.join(ART,'idx_mathlib')), **GRAPH_THRESHOLDS)
   out = arm_absent(al, blocks)
   print('total annotated blocks:', len(blocks))
   print('absent-arm n:', out['n'], 'status:', out['status'])
   print('already answerable from mathlib alone:', len(blocks) - out['n'])
   "

   Output: total annotated blocks = 179 (matches README:250's "179 annotated statements" --
   that figure IS current and correct, leave it alone). absent-arm n = 174 (matches the sum in
   the existing status table, so "174" itself is right). status = {matched: 0, ambiguous: 4,
   unmatched: 170} -- NOT 167/7/0 as documented. already-answerable-from-mathlib-alone = 5, not
   the 1 implied by "174 of 175".

Put together: the correct current denominator for line 252 is 179 (not 175), with 5 (not 1)
already answerable from mathlib alone, and the status breakdown at line 259 should read
"170 unmatched, 4 ambiguous, 0 matched" (not "167 unmatched, 7 ambiguous, 0 matched").
correct_abstention and false_match_rate are unaffected (still 100% / 0%, confirmed in the same
run).

This is presumably the same scanner-fix corpus growth documented at README:269 for the present
arm (idx_mathlib gained ~11k declarations too, so more of the 179 statements now coincidentally
already have their declaration in mathlib alone, shrinking the true-negative count and changing
the ambiguous/unmatched split). Whoever fixes this should sanity-check that story against
git blame / the scanner-fix commit rather than taking my inference on faith -- I did not
verify why the split moved from 167/7 to 170/4, only that it has.

Fix: rewrite README.md:250-259 to say "179 annotated statements" is the pool, "5 already have
an answer in mathlib alone" (not 1), the absent arm remains n=174 (unchanged, still correct),
and update the status table to 170 unmatched / 4 ambiguous / 0 matched.

Evidence that closes this: re-run the script above and confirm every number in the updated
paragraph matches its output.
close_reason: Fixed README.md:254-262 absent-arm section: reproduced the bead's script verbatim (179 total, absent-arm n=174, status 170 unmatched/4 ambiguous/0 matched, 5 already-answerable from mathlib alone), updated prose+table to match, left correct_abstention/false_match_rate unchanged as they were confirmed unaffected. Full suite: 76 tests, exactly the one known pre-existing failure (176!=175 in test_corpus.py, unrelated). See sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-1f3.md.

description:
The one pre-existing suite failure (per CLAUDE.md/handoff baseline) is real drift, not a broken corpus.

title: sandbox.sh: named uv-cache/uv-python volumes mount root-owned, breaking uv for the non-root worker user
description:
mathgraph-rq3 documented a workaround (UV_CACHE_DIR/UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR/XDG_DATA_HOME
pointed at /tmp) in sandbox-prompt.md's Environment section for a real bug:
the docker named volumes sandbox.sh mounts for uv caching come up root-owned,
so `uv run` fails immediately for the non-root `node` user every worker runs
as, unless the workaround is applied by hand.

Root cause, confirmed from inside a worker container (this repo's own
mathgraph-rq3 investigation):

  -v claude-uv-cache:/home/node/.cache/uv \
  -v claude-uv-python:/home/node/.local/share/uv/python \

in sandbox.sh's run_worker(). `ls -la /home/node/.cache` and
`/home/node/.local/share` show both mount points owned by root:root while
sibling non-mounted dirs (e.g. /home/node/.claude) are node:node -- i.e. the
named volumes are being initialized root-owned on first use, most likely
because the `claude` image doesn't pre-create those exact paths with `node`
ownership before the volume is first populated.

This bead is exactly the "fix the container image / volume" half of
mathgraph-rq3's two closing options, which mathgraph-rq3 deliberately did NOT
attempt: this sandbox has no `docker` binary, so any change to sandbox.sh's

title: uv cache/data dirs under /home/node owned by root, block 'uv run' for the default user without env overrides
description:
In this container, 'MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -m unittest discover tests' (the exact command sandbox-prompt.md's Environment section says to run) fails immediately with:

error: Failed to initialize cache at `/home/node/.cache/uv`
  Caused by: failed to open file `/home/node/.cache/uv/CACHEDIR.TAG`: Permission denied (os error 13)

Root cause: whoami is 'node', but /home/node/.cache/uv and /home/node/.local/share/uv (and their parents) are owned by root:root (drwxr-xr-x), not node -- confirmed with ls -la on both paths. So the default uv cache/python-install/data locations are read-only to the user the session actually runs as.

Workaround used this session to get the documented test command running at all:

  export UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/uv-cache UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/uv-python XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/xdg-data
  mkdir -p /tmp/uv-cache /tmp/uv-python /tmp/xdg-data
  MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -m unittest discover tests

With that workaround, all 76 tests pass in ~93s. Without it, a fresh session following sandbox-prompt.md's Environment section verbatim cannot run the suite at all, and might misdiagnose it as a real repo/dependency problem rather than a container permissions issue.

This is a container/image setup issue, not a repo code bug -- nothing in this repo's tree controls /home/node ownership. Filing it anyway because it's a reproducible blocker for the exact command the project's own agent instructions tell every fresh session to run.

What would close this: either fix the container image so /home/node/.cache and /home/node/.local/share are owned by the user the agent actually runs as (root vs node mismatch, likely a Dockerfile USER/chown ordering issue -- see ./Dockerfile), or add the UV_CACHE_DIR/UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR/XDG_DATA_HOME env-var workaround to sandbox-prompt.md's Environment section so it's not rediscovered every session.
